title: The remote that ate button presses
hints: Two questions. The handler only gets a `struct k_work *`, so how does it know which `struct button` that work item lives inside? And `k_work_submit` on an item that's already pending does nothing (it returns 0), so how many presses can one run of the handler stand for?

Recover the context with `struct button *b = CONTAINER_OF(work, struct button, work);`. Then don't handle "one press per run": the ISR counts `presses`, the handler counts `handled`, and the handler loops until they match. Never sleep in a work handler, because every other work item in the system waits behind you.

Handler: `struct button *b = CONTAINER_OF(work, struct button, work); while (b->handled < b->presses) { log_event(b); k_busy_wait(HANDLE_US); b->handled++; }`. `button_b_isr` is the same as A's: `btn_b.presses++; k_work_submit(&btn_b.work);`.
